- When sentiment is consistently low (≤0.4) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; cap forecast at +3% above peak or use 20-day moving average for stabilization.
- If sentiment is high (≥0.8) and price is trending up, model frequently overcorrects; apply downward bias of 0.5–1.5% to avoid overbought bias.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.4–0.8) and price shows mean reversion, model often fails to revert; use 10-day SMA as anchor for mid-range correction.
- For 30-day horizon, model tends to overestimate early in the forecast window; apply 1–2% downward adjustment for first 5–7 days.
- If sentiment history shows repeated “reversal” patterns (e.g., 0.8 → 0.2 → 0.8), model often misreads momentum; use sentiment-weighted average of last 3–5 days for smoothing.
